task.name: Unmeasured cost overwrites a story's recorded outcome, so approved work is reported as failed and an investigation is recommended for a dependency skip
task.story_text:
## Observed

A story whose work completed and whose review approved is reported to the operator as a failure
requiring root-cause investigation, because its cost could not be measured.

In one run a story ran preflight, planning and plan review for $0.47, was approved at plan review,
and was then skipped before development because the story it had been made to depend on failed. Three
surfaces describe that same story three different ways: the audit record carries a success outcome
with the phase it reached, the run summary carries an approval verdict with a skipped outcome code,
and the operator-facing status reports it as failed with a primary classification of
unknown-needs-RCA and a recommendation to run an LLM-assisted diagnosis.

Only one of those is actionable, and it is the wrong one. The story did not fail, nothing about it
requires diagnosis, and the recommended investigation would spend money establishing that a
dependency skip was a dependency skip. The reason the classifier could not do better is that the
story's cost was unknown, and unknown cost is being allowed to consume the outcome rather than sit
beside it.

The dependency relationship was recorded at dispatch — the scheduler injected the edge itself after
measuring a file collision — so the information needed to classify the skip correctly was present
throughout.

## Expected

How a unit of work ended and how well its cost was measured are separate facts, and one does not
overwrite the other. A story with a recorded outcome keeps that outcome regardless of whether its
spend could be attributed, and an unmeasured cost is reported as an accounting condition against the
run rather than as the story's result.

Where an outcome is known from the run's own records, it is reported from those records rather than
inferred by a classifier that lacks them. A classification of unknown is reserved for work whose end
state is genuinely unknown, so that the recommendation attached to it — investigate this — is only
ever attached to work that would benefit from investigation.

The surfaces that describe one unit of work agree about what happened to it. Where they cannot, the
disagreement is itself reported, because an operator reading one surface has no way to know the
others disagree.

## Diagnosis

**Observed symptom.** A story that was approved and then skipped for a dependency is displayed as
failed with an unknown-needs-RCA classification and a recommendation to run a paid diagnosis.

**Evidence.**

- Audit substrate row for the story: `outcome_success = 1`, `final_phase = PLAN_REVIEW`,
  `total_cost_usd = NULL`.
- Run summary for the same story: `verdict: APPROVE`, `outcome_code: skipped`.
- Operator status for the same story: failed, `primary: unknown_needs_rca`, with a recommendation to
  run diagnosis against it.
- The same run's log records the scheduler injecting the dependency edge after measuring a file
  collision between the two stories, and the blocking story failing before development.
- The run summary also records `status: cost_unknown` for the story, and the sprint total is reported
  as unmeasurable.

**Ruled out.** Not the dependency-skip machinery, which behaved correctly — the edge was measured,
recorded, and honoured. Not a missing outcome: two of the three surfaces carry a usable one. Not the
separately-tracked defect in which a budget skip is reported as a dependency skip; here the skip
genuinely was a dependency skip and the misreport is at the classification layer above it. Not
absence of the cost defect being known: unmeasured spend is tracked separately, but its effect on
outcome classification is not.

**Confirmed cause.** Outcome classification consumes cost as an input and degrades to unknown when
cost is absent, so an accounting gap propagates into the story's reported result and into the
operator action derived from it, rather than being reported alongside a result the run already knows.

**Affected code path.** Sprint outcome classification and its RCA labelling, the status rendering
that consumes it, and the summary and audit writers that record the same story's outcome in differing
forms.

**Fix-success criterion.** A story with a recorded outcome reports that outcome whether or not its
cost was measured; unmeasured cost is reported as an accounting condition rather than as a failure or
an investigation request; and the audit record, run summary and operator status agree about how a
given story ended.

handoff.summary: Traced the reported three-surface disagreement to two seams and fixed both. (1) sprint/audit.py's canonical projection loop overwrote a story row's outcome with the canonical terminal outcome (SKIPPED) but dropped the reason the sprint recorded with it, so an approved-then-dependency-skipped story reached sprint-rca.yaml as a bare SKIPPED; it now projects the canonical skip reason into the row's error, and never overwrites a cause the story itself recorded. (2) sprint/rca.py fell to unknown_needs_rca — whose recommendation buys an LLM diagnosis — for any skip it could not attribute; a recorded skip with no reason now classifies as the new skip_reason_unrecorded class, whose action sends the operator to the sprint log and states there is nothing to diagnose. Cost measurement is now reported as cost_accounting {measured, status: cost_unknown} beside the outcome and is never an input to classification, and a disagreement between the per-story audit (successful PLAN_REVIEW) and the summary (SKIPPED) is reported as an outcome_consistency block naming the summary outcome as authoritative. cli/sprint_digest.py routes the new class to SKIPPED / INTAKE and prints the accounting and inconsistency notes beside the row. RULESET_VERSION 11 -> 12 with the version-pin assertion updated. Verified the pre-fix repro (SKIPPED + cost None + no reason -> unknown_needs_rca + 'forge diagnose') and that it now classifies correctly end to end.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Steps 1, 2, and 4 target an already-correct path. With the proposed fixture, rca.py::_recorded_skip_reason and _signal_rule_hits already classify summary outcome SKIPPED plus error 'dependency failed: ...' as dependency_skip, and status_reader.py::_outcome_to_status already maps SKIPPED to skipped, independently of cost. The fixture therefore passes before any fix. The conflicting audit is created upstream in sprint/runner.py: scheduler branches call _set_outcome and _record_current_story_entry with SKIPPED, while _write_story_audit serializes the CoordinatorResult whose successful intermediate phase may still be PLAN_REVIEW. runner.py and that caller/data flow are absent from the plan, so the audit/substrate disagreement can remain unchanged.
  Suggestion: Make Step 1 reproduce the scheduler path through run_sprint or a focused runner seam, then include sprint/runner.py and define how the canonical scheduler outcome and skip reason are projected into the terminal per-story audit and SQLite substrate while retaining PLAN_REVIEW only as the phase reached and cost_unknown only as accounting metadata.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 treats verdict and final_phase as fields that can identify an end state. In the reported case, verdict APPROVE and final_phase PLAN_REVIEW are explicitly intermediate facts; the terminal run outcome is SKIPPED. Making those fields authoritative can preserve the same cross-surface conflict or incorrectly turn a dependency skip into success.
  Suggestion: Define explicit precedence: canonical terminal sprint outcome/outcome_code and recorded skip reason determine how the story ended; verdict and final_phase describe approval and progress only. Conflicting intermediate fields should feed the inconsistency report, not terminal classification.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 6 says 'modify tests/cli/test_sprint_digest.py' and Step 1 creates 'tests/sprint/test_cost_unknown_outcome_classification.py', but tests/ is a flat layout (no tests/cli/ or tests/sprint/ packages) and no test_sprint_digest.py exists. Existing coverage for this area lives in tests/test_sprint_rca.py, tests/test_sprint_rca_skip_context.py and tests/test_sprint_digest_skip_categories.py.
  Suggestion: Place the new regression at tests/test_sprint_rca_cost_unknown_outcome.py (flat, matching CONVENTIONS.md naming) and extend tests/test_sprint_digest_skip_categories.py rather than creating tests/cli/ and tests/sprint/ subpackages.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5 adds a new field to the RCA payload, but rca.py carries SCHEMA_VERSION=1/RULESET_VERSION=11 and tests/test_sprint_rca.py:1305-1343 asserts version pinning and --check reproducibility against the emitted mapping.
  Suggestion: Bump RULESET_VERSION when classification behaviour or payload shape changes, and update the version-pinning assertions in tests/test_sprint_rca.py in the same change.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3's 'add or preserve a separate accounting status field' may touch the persisted summary/audit shape, which tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py polices.
  Suggestion: Prefer reusing story_budget.STATUS_UNKNOWN ('cost_unknown', story_budget.py:82) as the existing accounting signal; if a new field is genuinely needed, register it with the audit schema guard.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Preflight could not locate the site where absent cost degrades a known outcome; status_reader._outcome_to_status already maps SKIPPED to 'skipped' and rca's dependency_skip precedence (#2312, rca.py:1582-1595) already fires, so the live defect may be in a surface none of the listed steps names (e.g. the run-summary outcome writer in sprint/runner.py:4424/4555 or audit.py:1301, which derive outcome_code).
  Suggestion: Have the dev reproduce the three-surface scenario first (Step 1) and follow the failing surface, treating the Step 2-5 file list as a starting point rather than an exhaustive one; sprint/runner.py and sprint/audit.py outcome_code derivation are the most likely additional sites.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Make recorded story outcome authoritative and keep cost measurement status as separate accounting metadata. Harden RCA/status/summary rendering so dependency skips with unknown cost remain skipped, and add a consistency warning when audit, summary, and operator-facing status disagree.

steps.description: Add a focused regression fixture for an approved story skipped by a failed dependency with unknown cost.
steps.details: Construct the three-surface scenario from the spec: audit-style outcome_success=1/final_phase=PLAN_REVIEW/total_cost_usd=None, summary verdict APPROVE/outcome_code skipped/status cost_unknown, and an injected dependency_skip reason. Assert the operator classification is skipped/dependency_skip, not failed/unknown_needs_rca, and that no diagnosis recommendation is emitted.

steps.description: Make RCA classification prefer recorded outcome and skip reason before considering cost accounting state.
steps.details: In build_sprint_rca/_classify_story, ensure known terminal outcome fields and existing skip-reason precedence drive primary classification. Treat cost_unknown or total_cost_usd=None only as auxiliary accounting metadata; never let it select unknown_needs_rca when outcome_code, verdict, final_phase, or dependency_skip evidence already identifies the end state.

steps.description: Preserve cost_unknown as run-level accounting information in summary/audit output without changing story outcome.
steps.details: Keep existing cost_unknown reporting for unmeasurable spend, but audit the writer paths so missing total_cost_usd does not rewrite outcome_success, outcome_code, verdict, or final_phase. If needed, add or preserve a separate accounting status field beside the story outcome and sprint total measurability fields.

steps.description: Align operator-facing status rendering with the authoritative classification.
steps.details: Ensure status display maps dependency_skip/SKIPPED to skipped rather than failed, and suppress LLM diagnosis recommendations for dependency skips and other known non-failure outcomes even when accounting metadata says cost_unknown.

steps.description: Report disagreement between audit, summary, and operator status instead of silently choosing the worst-looking surface.
steps.details: Where these surfaces are combined, compare the recorded outcome signals used by RCA/status. If they conflict, include an explicit inconsistency/diagnostic field or status note while still preferring the run's recorded outcome over cost-derived unknown classification.

steps.description: Cover the affected seams with integration-level assertions.
steps.details: Extend the regression to exercise summary-to-RCA-to-status/digest flow, asserting that the audit record, run summary, and operator status all describe the story as skipped for dependency reasons, with cost_unknown reported separately and no RCA recommendation.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A story with a recorded outcome reports that outcome whether or not its cost was measured.
Unmeasured cost is reported as an accounting condition rather than as a failure or an investigation request.
Where an outcome is known from the run's own records, it is reported from those records rather than inferred by a classifier that lacks them.
A classification of unknown is reserved for work whose end state is genuinely unknown, so investigate recommendations only attach to work that benefits from investigation.
The audit record, run summary and operator status agree about how a given story ended.
Where surfaces cannot agree, the disagreement is itself reported.

risks.description: Preflight did not locate the exact path where cost_unknown becomes unknown_needs_rca.
risks.mitigation: Start with the regression fixture and trace the failing assertion through existing build_sprint_rca, _classify_story, audit writer, status_reader, and sprint_digest paths before changing broader behavior.

risks.description: Surface schemas may not currently have a dedicated place for cross-surface inconsistency.
risks.mitigation: Use the smallest existing diagnostic/status-note mechanism if one exists; otherwise add a narrowly scoped field consumed only by status/RCA output, without weakening validation boundaries.
